Working notes — inventory ordering
- One SKU; decide daily order quantity. Cost is dominated by stockouts/lost sales; holding/order costs are small. High costs occurred on stockout days: Day4 7.00, Day6 5.50, Day9 4.00.
- Lead time: orders arrive about 2 days after placement. Example: order 8 on Day3 appeared as arriving Day5. Plan for demand during lead time, not just current stock.
- Demand is volatile but frequent: last 9 observed sales were 8,5,4,1,7,1,7,7,0. Mean ~4.4, recent cluster around 7. Plan with ~5-7/day and safety for occasional 8.
- Reorder rule: track inventory position = on-hand + inbound. Keep position >= ~14 units (2 days x ~6-7 + safety). If below, order up to ~18-20. Do not wait until stock is 0-5; the Day3 order came too late to prevent Day4 stockout.
- Check listed inbound before ordering; avoid duplicate/overordering. Day10 had 0 on hand but 11 inbound; ordering 9 may be reasonable to cover the lead-time gap.
- Ops notes (forklift certification, temp, carrier pickup, cycle count) have not affected demand or arrivals; ignore unless evidence shows delay.
- Submit an integer every day. Blank or 0 when stock is low is risky; order earlier when position falls below target.

Working notes — inventory ordering
- One SKU, daily integer order. Stockout/lost-sales cost dominates; holding/order costs are minor. Recent stockouts were severe: Days16–20 costs 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 7.5, 11.5. Consecutive zero-on-hand days are the main failure.
- Lead time ~2 days. Plan demand over full lead time plus safety, not just current stock. Having inbound [5,9] while on hand is 0 is still too thin.
- Demand: last 14 = 1,7,7,0,8,3,5,5,5,9,6,5,9,6. Mean ~5.4, but recent cluster is 5–9, max 9, occasional 0–3. Plan ~8/day and safety 5–8. Do not rely on earlier ~4.4 mean.
- Reorder rule: inventory position = on-hand + inbound. Target position ~24–30. If below, order up to ~30–35, biased upward because stockout cost >> holding cost.
- Do not wait for stock 0–3. Build buffer before demand spikes. Day20 with 0 on hand and inbound [5,9] needed more than 6 units.
- Order every day the position is below target; small orders like 5–6 leave stockout exposure. Avoid blank/0 unless position is already above target.
- Check inbound before ordering to avoid duplicates, but small inbound should not justify a low order.
- Ops notes (counts, temp, carrier, forklift, cycle count) have not affected demand/arrivals; ignore unless evidence shows delay.
- Submit an integer daily.

Working notes — inventory ordering
- One SKU, daily integer order. Stockout/lost-sales cost dominates; holding/order costs minor. Consecutive zero-on-hand days remain the main failure.
- Demand has shifted higher again. Last 14 at Day30: 6,5,9,6,5,9,6,13,8,8,12,15,7,10. Mean ~8.5; recent 7 mean ~10.4, max 15. Plan ~10/day, safety 8–12. Do not rely on older ~5.4 or ~8/day.
- Lead time ~2 days. Ordering today cannot fix today’s stockout. Need positive on-hand buffer before spikes. On hand 0 with inbound [6,20] still cost 11.5; inbound [5,9] is too thin.
- Inventory position = on-hand + inbound. Target position ~35–40. If below, order up to ~35–40; bias upward because stockout >> holding. Small orders like 8–9 when position is low leave exposure.
- Blank/0 order only if position is already at/above target. Day29 blank with position 28 cost 0.30, acceptable; Day24 blank with position 16 cost 1.30 and was too low.
- Check inbound before ordering to avoid duplicates, but small near-term inbound should not justify a low order. Avoid waiting for stock 0–3. Build buffer before demand spikes.
- Ops notes (temp, cycle count, forklift, racking, carrier) have not affected demand/arrivals; ignore unless evidence shows delay.
- Submit an integer daily.

Working notes — inventory ordering
- One SKU daily integer. Cost ≈ 0.1 per ending on-hand unit + 0.5 fixed if order >0. Stockout still costly, but recent high costs came from overstock holding, not stockouts.
- Demand: last 14 at Day40: 12,15,7,10,14,3,4,3,6,5,3,0,4,2. Mean ~6.3; last 7 ~3.3, max 15. Use ~6–7/day with spikes, not old ~10.4 or ~5.4. Volatile.
- Lead time 2 days. Arrivals list [today,tomorrow]; orders placed today arrive in 2 days. Position = on-hand + listed inbound. Ordering cannot fix today.
- Target inventory position ~20–25. This covers ~2-day mean (12–14) plus safety 8–10. Do not target 35–40: Days31–40 show positions 31–40 led to holding 2.3–3.7/day; extra orders just add 0.5.
- Order only if position is below target; order up to target. If position at/above target, order 0. Avoid small top-up orders near target (fixed 0.5 cost).
- Bias slightly upward only when position is low or demand spike risk is high; but do not build >30 on-hand without need.
- Check inbound before ordering. Ignore ops notes (carrier, temp, forklift, racking, cycle count); no evidence they affect demand/arrivals.
- Submit integer daily.
